import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Quick feature selection using Welch's t-test
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if len(feats.x[:, i].shape) == 1:
            t_stat = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==0, i], feats.x[feats.y==1, i], equal_var=False)[0])
            t_stats.append((fid, t_stat))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic and take top features
    t_stats.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    top_features = [fid for fid, _ in t_stats[:20]]  # Limit to top 20 for efficiency
    
    # Remove near-duplicates quickly
    representative_features = set()
    used_features = set()
    
    # Create correlation matrix for quick lookup
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    for fid in top_features:
        if fid in used_features:
            continue
            
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        # Find correlated features (|r| >= 0.6)
        correlated = []
        for other_fid in top_features:
            if other_fid == fid or other_fid in used_features:
                continue
            other_col_idx = feats.column(other_fid)
            corr_val = corr_matrix[col_idx, other_col_idx]
            if abs(corr_val) >= 0.6:
                correlated.append(other_fid)
        
        # Add the feature with highest t-statistic in the group
        if correlated:
            # Include the current feature and its strongest correlated partner
            representative_features.add(fid)
            # Mark correlated features as used
            for cfid in correlated:
                used_features.add(cfid)
        else:
            representative_features.add(fid)
        used_features.add(fid)
    
    # If no features selected, return empty design
    if not representative_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select final top features by t-statistic
    final_features = []
    for fid in representative_features:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        t_stat = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx], 
                                   feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx], 
                                   equal_var=False)[0])
        final_features.append((fid, t_stat))
    
    final_features.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Select drivers (up to MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = tuple(fid for fid, _ in final_features[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Build columns and products
    columns = tuple(fid for fid, _ in final_features)
    
    # Look for interaction terms among top features (limited to prevent overfitting)
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns[:10]):  # Limit to top 10 features
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(columns[i+1:10], i+1):
            # Check if features are uncorrelated
            col1_idx = feats.column(fid1)
            col2_idx = feats.column(fid2)
            corr_val = corr_matrix[col1_idx, col2_idx]
            if abs(corr_val) < 0.5:  # Only add interaction if not highly correlated
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Simple weighted score based on standardized values
    loadings = {}
    for fid in columns:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        t_stat = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx], 
                                   feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx], 
                                   equal_var=False)[0])
        loadings[fid] = t_stat
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
